# Capstone build spec: the kitchen-sink Tour of Heroes This is the conformance target for the capstone build. It is intent plus decisions, not pixels: a low-fidelity layout, build guidelines, a theme palette, and an icon scheme. Build to this with the real sealed spartan primitives and the MVVM pattern, under all gates. Do NOT chase a pixel-perfect mock. `prototype/tour-of-heroes.html` is a colour-and-mood reference ONLY. It is known to be non-responsive (measured: 19 responsive-gate violations) and its CSS and layout mechanics must not be copied. Take the look and feel from it; take the structure, palette, icons, and responsive rules from this document. ## How to use this - The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo. - Build every screen responsive-correct at 375px, 768px, and 1280px. The Part 5 responsive gate is on: no horizontal page scroll, no element escaping the viewport, no clipped content at any of the three widths. This is the bar the mock failed and the build must clear. - Use spartan primitives for everything that has one. Compose, do not hand-roll. The sealing gate enforces this once the vocabulary is expanded. ## Theme palette A cool indigo-biased neutral set with an amber-gold action colour and a permanently-dark navigation rail. Apply these to the existing spartan CSS tokens in `src/styles.css` (the `:root` and `:root.dark` blocks). 1 --- 2 name: house-style 3 description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. 4 --- 5 6 # House frontend conventions 7 8 These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. 9 10 ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet 11 12 A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 13 14 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 15 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 16 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 17 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 18 5. **Utilities live in `@apply`, and every rule below still applies to them.** Semantic color tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions, appearance never on a primitive. Moving a utility from the template into `@apply` does not change whether it is allowed. 19 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. 20 21 Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. 22 23 ```html 24 25

Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. --- # House frontend conventions These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 5. **Utilities live in `@apply`, and every rule below still applies to them.** Semantic color tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions, appearance never on a primitive. Moving a utility from the template into `@apply` does not change whether it is allowed. 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. content.text:
The console is integrated and builds. Every navigation destination now renders a real screen, and the screens share one set of state. An edit on the dossier shows on the roster and dashboard, and deploys, recruits, retires and containments propagate the same way.

**What changed**

- **Placeholders replaced.** Missions, Threats, Recruit and Settings are real screens, each with its own ViewModel (no `providedIn`, provided on the component, no `.subscribe`).
  - **Missions:** live deployments with Stand down, plus heroes ready to deploy.
  - **Threats:** the threat board, open threats first, with a Contain action.
  - **Recruit:** a zod-driven intake form. It adds a hero on Reserve with a fresh id (HRO-0082 in the first session) and opens their dossier.
  - **Settings:** a theme preference (match system, light, dark) that persists.
- **Shared state.** Deploy goes through a new `MissionService`, so the dashboard's "Missions live" tile and the Missions screen agree. Retiring a hero also stands down their missions. The dashboard's "Open threats" comes from the same `ThreatService` as the Threats screen.
- **Duplicates removed.** `initialsOf`, the status-variant map and the roster-row shaping were copied into two ViewModels and a component, and now live once in `domain/hero.presentation.ts`. The hero field definitions are shared by the edit and recruit schemas.
- **Dead links fixed.** The top-bar search was inert. It now navigates to `/roster?q=…`, and the roster reads that query. The dashboard also gained the roster table the spec calls for.

**Verification**

- `ng build` compiles. The only warnings are the bundle-budget ones that were already there.
- `npm run lint`, `check:contrast`, `check:boot` (7 routes), `check:responsive` (375/768/1280) and `check:interaction` all pass.
- `ng test`: 2 of 2 pass.
- A throwaway Playwright check of 15 cross-screen flows passes with no console errors. It lives in `%TEMP%`, outside the repo. It navigates in-app, because a full page reload resets the in-memory state.

**Not done, and why**

- `npm run check:wiring` can't run: the script points at `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs`, which isn't in this repo.
- The shell template (`app.html`) still uses Tailwind utility classes in its markup. That drift came from an earlier stage, and converting it to BEM is a separate refactor. Lint doesn't flag it.
- The notifications bell is still inert. There is no notification feed to show.
- Edits, deploys, recruits and containments last only until the page reloads, as the existing pages already state.

I haven't committed anything.
